results.name: Tyre Hammering
instructions: Stand in front of a tyre holding a sledgehammer, feet shoulder-width apart.
Swing the hammer up over one shoulder.
Bring it down forcefully onto the tyre, bending your knees as you strike.
Control the rebound and repeat, switching sides regularly.
tips: Slide your top hand down the handle as you strike.
Keep your back flat.
results.description: Tyre Hammering is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a hammer, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals, Lats, Forearms.

results.name: Unilateral Box Jump - Bilateral Deceleration
instructions: Stand on one leg in front of a box.
Jump onto the box from one leg.
Land on both feet, absorbing the landing with bent knees and hips.
Step down and repeat, alternating the take-off leg.
tips: Land softly and quietly.
Choose a box height you can land on in control.
results.description: Unilateral Box Jump - Bilateral Deceleration is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Hamstrings.

results.name: Unilateral Box Jump
instructions: Stand on one leg in front of a low box.
Bend your standing knee and swing your arms back.
Jump onto the box, landing softly on the same leg.
Step down and repeat, then switch legs.
tips: Start with a very low box.
Land with your knee over your toes.
results.description: Unilateral Box Jump is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Hamstrings, Core.

results.name: Unilateral Front Plank
instructions: Start in a forearm plank with your body in a straight line.
Lift one leg a few inches off the floor.
Hold without letting your hips rotate or sag.
Switch legs after the set time.
tips: Squeeze the glute of the raised leg.
Keep your hips square to the floor.
results.description: Unilateral Front Plank is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Shoulders.

results.name: Unilateral Jumps
instructions: Stand on one leg with a slight bend in the knee.
Hop forward or straight up on the same leg.
Land softly, absorbing the landing.
Repeat, then switch legs.
tips: Stick each landing before the next hop.
Use your arms for balance.
results.description: Unilateral Jumps is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Core.

results.name: Unilateral Plank
instructions: Start in a high plank.
Lift one arm and the opposite leg off the floor.
Hold the position with your hips level.
Return and switch sides.
tips: Widen your supporting base if you lose balance.
Keep your neck in line with your spine.
results.description: Unilateral Plank is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Shoulders.

results.name: Walking Fast
instructions: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart and your arms relaxed by your sides.
Step forward with your right foot, rolling through the heel to the ball of your foot while swinging your left arm forward and right arm back.
Push off with your right foot, quickly bringing your left foot forward to step, swinging your right arm forward and left arm back. Increase your pace while maintaining control.
Continue this alternating pattern, maintaining a brisk and consistent stride. Repeat for the desired distance or time.
tips: Maintain a brisk pace that challenges you but allows you to walk efficiently.
Wear comfortable, supportive shoes to prevent injury and enhance your walking experience.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid tensing your upper body.
results.description: Walking Fast is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Core, Lower Back, Hip Flexors.

results.name: Walking
instructions: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart and your arms relaxed by your sides.
Step forward with your right foot, rolling through the heel to the ball of your foot while swinging your left arm forward and right arm back.
Push off with your right foot, bringing your left foot forward to step, swinging your right arm forward and left arm back.
Continue this alternating pattern, maintaining a natural stride and rhythm. Repeat for the desired distance or time.
tips: Swing your arms naturally in opposition to your legs to help with balance and momentum.
Maintain a steady and comfortable pace that allows you to walk efficiently.
Wear comfortable, supportive shoes to prevent injury and enhance your walking experience.
results.description: Walking is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Core, Lower Back, Hip Flexors.

results.name: Archer Push Up
instructions: Start in a push-up position with your hands placed wider than shoulder-width apart and your body forming a straight line from head to heels.
Bend your right elbow to lower your chest towards your right hand while keeping your left arm extended straight to the side.
Push back up to the starting position.
Bend your left elbow to lower your chest towards your left hand while keeping your right arm extended straight to the side. Continue alternating sides.
tips: Ensure your shoulders and hips stay level to avoid any imbalance during the movement.
Use a slow and steady breathing pattern, exhaling as you push up and inhaling as you lower down.
Keep your gaze slightly forward to maintain a neutral spine and avoid neck strain.
results.description: Archer Push Up is an advanced multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

results.name: Assisted Weighted Push Up
instructions: Position yourself in a high plank position with your hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, your feet together, and your body forming a straight line from head to heels. Have your partner place a weight plate on your upper back.
Lower your body towards the floor by bending your elbows, until your chest nearly touches the floor.
Push through your palms to straighten your arms and return to the starting position, maintaining a controlled and steady movement. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Maintain a straight line from head to heels to ensure proper form.
Exhale as you push up and inhale as you lower your body.
Ensure the weight plate is securely placed on your upper back for safety.
results.description: Assisted Weighted Push Up is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Shoulders, Core.
